comment: Experiment for 0.5.0 (extra_operations: HOVER), written without access to the site: probe before trusting the outcomes. The jQuery UI menu opens its submenu on hover and, as far as I know, on click as well, so both arms of an A/B may pass here; what this spec measures is whether Jev chooses HOVER when it is offered and what offering it does to the other steps. A menu that opens on :hover only (most site navigation bars) is the case HOVER exists for: add one from an application of your own. Probed 2026-11-17: the first pass statement ('heading says JQuery UI ... Menus are tricky to automate') was already true of the menu page itself ('JQueryUI - Menu', and its paragraph says menus are an automation challenge), so the pass was pending at step 1 with no action and every run ended assert_failed on the url. The pass now names what only the landing page shows, and needs the click (`after`). The submenu opens 300 ms after the pointer arrives (jQuery UI's delay), which 0.5.0's HOVER did not wait for (flagged NO-EFFECT); fixed in 0.6.0.
goal: Open the Enabled menu by hovering over it and choose 'Back to JQuery UI' from the submenu it opens, so that the JQuery UI page is shown.
notes: The submenu appears only while the pointer is over Enabled.

back_on_jquery_ui.when: The page heading reads 'JQuery UI' and the text says JQuery UI's set of Widgets causes automation challenges, with a 'Menu' link below it
